author: refuter
recommendation: A guard present on one read entry point but absent on a sibling read entry point is only a finding when the candidate names an in-scope consumer that actually reads the unguarded entry point and the concrete state-changing divergence that follows; a view function with no traced caller yields speculative harm contingent on unshown third-party code.

author: refuter
recommendation: A claim that a caller-side proportional computation over-claims from a shared pool must show the callee's accounting path actually paying out the excess without an underflow or apportionment check, since a per-entity view struct that is already debited at split time makes the ratio correct and leaves the alleged loss unproven.

author: refuter
recommendation: A permissionless entry point on a delegatecall-only helper or library target is not exploitable unless the candidate shows that the assets or authority it manipulates are actually held at the address where the code executes on the attacker's call path, rather than at the caller that normally delegatecalls into it.

author: refuter
recommendation: An unguarded intermediate hop in a multi-leg swap is not a finding when a downstream check bounds the cumulative final output, unless the candidate identifies the concrete unprivileged entry point through which a non-owner supplies that downstream guard parameter and shows the authorization check is absent in the code presented.

author: refuter
recommendation: A claim that a not-yet-settled position is mispriced by a live rate must point to code within the reviewed scope that actually freezes the underlying entitlement at request time, and must show a divergence the unprivileged actor can control or amplify rather than a bounded accrual over a protocol-fixed window that any party can permissionlessly collapse.

author: refuter
recommendation: A claim that a missing guard permanently freezes funds must demonstrate that the precondition state is reachable by an unprivileged actor, and must survive the fact that the same unguarded assumption on the state-creating path causes that path to revert before the state can ever be established.

author: refuter
recommendation: A claim that a proportional multi-asset payout floors to zero must demonstrate that the required extreme reserve imbalance is actually reachable by permissionless trading against the pool's invariant — not merely asserted via "flash-swap" — and must identify a trigger callable by someone other than the position owner, since a state only the owner can enter at their own expense is griefing, not an external exploit.

author: refuter
recommendation: A claim that a valuation function mis-scales a quantity must exhibit, from the presented code, a concrete path where the caller-supplied amount and the accounting denominator it is divided against are updated by different quantities; if every mutation shown adjusts both sides by the same amount, and the divergence would have to occur inside an external component whose code is not presented, the mismatch is unproven.

author: refuter
recommendation: A mid-transaction-state (reentrancy-window) pricing claim must quote the external contract's actual state-mutation ordering around the callback and show that the resulting error has the sign required by the stated exploit direction, and that the callback exists in the contract shape the consumer can actually be deployed against.

author: refuter
recommendation: A manipulation claim against a value produced by an inherited or otherwise unshown routine must trace that routine's actual arithmetic and any deviation-tolerance check it applies, and must demonstrate with the code's own configured bounds that the manipulation-induced shift in the cross-check input stays inside them, rather than asserting the sanity band is satisfied.

author: refuter
recommendation: A missing-check finding on a read-only view getter requires the candidate to name a concrete in-scope state-mutating consumer that actually calls that specific getter; when the guarded sibling getter is the documented integration surface and the unguarded ones exist only to satisfy an inherited interface, an unconsumed gap is hardening advice, not an exploit.

author: refuter
recommendation: A denial-of-service claim resting on a sanity-check revert must quote the actual comparison, threshold, and units from the code that implements the check rather than asserting them, and must show the revert condition is reachable by ordinary or cheaply-forced state rather than being the fail-closed guard operating as designed.

author: refuter
recommendation: A claim that an attacker can force an alternate valuation branch must identify the concrete state transition that flips the branch predicate and show it is reachable by the attacker before the valuation is read, rather than pointing at a post-check hook whose own code documents it as a no-op when that state is absent.

author: refuter
recommendation: A valuation branch that a position holder triggers only for their own position, and that switches pricing to track collateral the holder demonstrably moved into a different accounting bucket, is intended accounting unless the candidate exhibits a concrete divergence between the two pricing paths for the identical underlying claim and names the unprivileged mechanism that forces the branch onto a third party.

author: refuter
recommendation: A size-agnostic state flag is only a finding if the candidate names the unprivileged call path that actually sets the flag with a mismatched magnitude AND shows the resulting valuation error runs in the attacker's favour rather than against their own position.

author: refuter
recommendation: A valuation-branch-switching claim must show that the alternate branch actually returns a larger number than the default one and that the state needed to trigger it does not itself trip an all-elements consistency check that the trigger condition only tests existentially.

author: refuter
recommendation: a reentrancy or stale-read claim must identify a callback into attacker-controlled code that is actually reachable on the traced path, consistent with the branch predicates the guard has already fixed and with the literal arguments the calling frame passes, rather than borrowing a callback from a sibling branch that the same guard excludes.

author: refuter
recommendation: A claim that a stored snapshot quantity can be outgrown by a later-supplied amount must identify the concrete unprivileged call path that increases the tracked quantity while the snapshot is frozen, and must show the downstream accounting component that actually settles the transfer does not independently re-bound the amount against its own stored record.

author: refuter
recommendation: A claim that an internal helper "trusts" a caller-supplied flag must identify the external entry point and the concrete unprivileged calldata path that makes the flag diverge from the state it should mirror; when the calling code that computes the flag is not exhibited, the trust assumption is unproven and the finding fails.

author: refuter
recommendation: A reentrancy claim must identify a concrete point inside the alleged window where attacker-controlled code actually receives execution; a value transfer whose recipient is the protocol's own contract with an inert fallback hands control to the protocol, not to any external party, and configuration-fixed callees do not supply that entry point.

author: refuter
recommendation: A denomination-mismatch claim must point to the concrete line where the mismatched quantity feeds a pooled, supply-wide valuation shared by non-acting participants; if the mismatched pair is only ever stored and prorated within the acting party's own earmarked request, the loss is self-inflicted, not socialised, and the claim fails.

author: refuter
recommendation: A claim that a native-asset unwrap/wrap step operates on the wrong balance must be refuted when the contract's own constructor-time index/role assignment forces the unwrapped bucket to coincide with the accounted leg in every configuration where that bucket exists, and the only surviving variant is a deterministic revert in a deployer-chosen configuration whose triggering behavior lives in code not presented for review.

author: refuter
recommendation: A claim that a value-bearing leg is booked without backing must identify, in code, both the registry/lookup path that actually resolves to a live counterparty for that leg and the counterparty logic that credits an amount it never received — a lookup that resolves to a codeless address reverts the whole call, and a lookup that resolves only via operator registration is privileged configuration.

author: refuter
recommendation: A denial-of-service claim must show that the blocking precondition cannot be restored by any permissionless, dust-cost action a third party can take atomically in the same transaction as the blocked call; if a freely transferable asset or public state can be seeded by the caller to satisfy the failing check, the claimed permanence and its severity collapse.

author: refuter
recommendation: A constructor-set immutable integration parameter is privileged configuration, so a candidate alleging harm from a wrong value must name the unprivileged action that induces or changes that value rather than assuming the deployer already chose an out-of-domain one.

author: refuter
recommendation: A behavioral divergence that can only arise from a deployment-time pairing of an integration target with an interface variant, both fixed in immutable constructor configuration, counts as privileged configuration unless the candidate identifies an unprivileged action that induces the mismatch and demonstrates the external counterparty's differing behavior rather than assuming it.

author: refuter
recommendation: a claim whose damaging step occurs in code outside the reviewed unit must trace that step in the actual shown code, and must identify an unprivileged trigger rather than a deployment-time pairing of parameters chosen by a trusted deployer
